scope: Theorem 1.1 (Area law) of the manuscript “A two-dimensional area law from a global spectral gap” (preprints/A-two-dimensional-area-law-from-a-global-spectral-gap-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 265 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 91e272a2245ad0bd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every q, R, J as above and every ∆ > 0, there is a finite constant C = C(q, R, J, ∆) with the following property. Suppose that Λ is a finite induced square-lattice domain and that the Hamiltonian (1.1) has a unique normalized ground vector Ω, up to phase, with ground energy E0, and satisfies H − E0 id ≥ ∆ (︁ id −|Ω⟩⟨Ω| )︁ . Then for every A ⊆ Λ, SΩ(A) ≤ C |∂ΛA|. (1.2) The same constant applies to all such domains, sets, and Hamiltonians.
